definitions.explanation: The kitchen area of a traditional Japanese restaurant where food is prepared. Named after the wooden boards ({板|いた}) used in the workspace.
By extension, refers to the person who works in the kitchen — the chef or cook of a Japanese restaurant.

examples.japanese: {板場|いたば}で{魚|さかな}をさばく。
examples.english: To fillet fish in the kitchen.

examples.japanese: {板場|いたば}は{忙|いそが}しい{時間帯|じかんたい}に{入|はい}ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not enter the kitchen during busy hours.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{板場|いたば}は{二十年|にじゅうねん}の{経験|けいけん}を{持|も}つベテランだ。
examples.english: The chef at this restaurant is a veteran with twenty years of experience.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{若|わか}くして{板場|いたば}を{任|まか}されている。
examples.english: Despite his youth, he has been entrusted with the kitchen.

examples.japanese: {修業|しゅぎょう}{時代|じだい}は{板場|いたば}の{下働|したばたら}きから{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: During his apprenticeship, he started from the bottom in the kitchen.

examples.japanese: あの{料亭|りょうてい}の{板場|いたば}さんは{腕|うで}がいい。
examples.english: The chef at that traditional restaurant is very skilled.

notes:
Specifically associated with traditional Japanese cuisine ({和食|わしょく}) and Japanese-style restaurants. Not used for Western-style kitchens.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {板場|いたば}に{立|た}つ: to stand in the kitchen (i.e., to work as a chef)
- {板場|いたば}を{任|まか}される: to be entrusted with the kitchen
- {板場|いたば}さん: the chef (colloquial, respectful)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {台所|だいどころ} / キッチン: kitchen — general terms for any kitchen
- {厨房|ちゅうぼう}: kitchen (professional) — used for restaurant kitchens of any cuisine
- {板前|いたまえ}: Japanese cuisine chef — refers specifically to the person, more common than {板場|いたば} in sense 2
- {料理人|りょうりにん}: cook, chef — general term for any professional cook
